key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr delivered the lowest measured wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising option for protecting 304 stainless steel components exposed to both sliding wear and corrosion.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation, HVOF and HVAF spraying.
Compare coating microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction and volumetric wear.
Evaluate corrosion behavior and examine wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF reduced volumetric wear rate from (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for bare steel to (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) and showed the lowest corrosion current density, (1.75±0.02) µA/cm², among the coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
